headline: April CPI Accelerates to 2.8% on Record 28.6% Gasoline Spike as BoC Holds at 2.25%

discovery_stats.new_this_week_note: projects_all.json carries no discovered_at/date_discovered field; weekly-new count not derivable from this export

facts.statement: Canada's headline CPI accelerated to +2.8% year-over-year in April 2026, the highest in roughly two years, up from +2.4% in March, driven by a record +28.6% year-over-year gasoline increase. Core CPI (median + trim average) eased to 2.1% from 2.3% and CPI ex-gasoline slowed to +2.0%.
facts.source_title: Statistics Canada — Consumer Price Index, April 2026
connections: Gasoline pass-through tied to WTI at US$103.02/bbl (+64.33% YoY) amid the Strait of Hormuz disruption
59 oil_gas projects ($97.58B) and 613 transport_logistics projects ($44.13B) exposed to fuel-cost dynamics

facts.statement: The Bank of Canada held the overnight rate at 2.25% on April 29, 2026, a fourth consecutive hold, citing the Middle East war and U.S. tariff uncertainty; the Council stated it will not let higher energy prices become persistent inflation.
facts.source_title: Bank of Canada — Maintains policy rate at 2.25%
connections: 211 residential projects ($32.23B) and 1,678 infrastructure projects ($210.26B) are rate-sensitive
Prime rate held at 6.09%; GoC 2Y at 3.07%, 10Y at 3.70% — yields well above the policy rate

facts.statement: Real GDP contracted -0.6% annualized in Q4 2025; full-year 2025 growth was +1.7%, the slowest since 2020. A Q1 2026 advance estimate shows +0.4%, with the official Q1 release scheduled for May 29, 2026.
facts.source_title: Statistics Canada — GDP, income and expenditure, Q4 2025
connections: Manufacturing GDP -3.1% YoY; the database tracks 38 manufacturing projects ($62.19B)
Inventory withdrawal and weak exports the principal Q4 drags

facts.statement: Canada posted a +C$1.8B merchandise trade surplus in March 2026, the first since September 2025, as exports rose +8.5% to C$72.8B (energy +15.6%, crude +18.9%, metals/minerals +24%); imports fell -1.6%. The surplus with the U.S. widened to C$7.1B.
facts.source_title: Statistics Canada — Canadian international merchandise trade, March 2026
connections: Crude/energy export strength aligns with 59 oil_gas projects ($97.58B) and 390 mining projects ($227.11B)
2025 IEEPA tariffs ended following a February 2026 U.S. Supreme Court ruling

facts.statement: Canadian housing starts jumped +17% in April 2026 to a 279,317 SAAR from 239,747 in March, exceeding a ~240,000 estimate; the six-month trend rose +3.2% to 256,777. Toronto starts +34% YoY, Montreal +21%, multi-unit driven.
connections: 211 residential projects ($32.23B) and 72 NAICS-23 construction projects ($9.96B) tracked
Construction GDP -0.5% m/m, +2.8% YoY despite the starts rebound

facts.statement: The April Labour Force Survey showed unemployment rising +0.2pp to 6.9% with employment down -18,000 (-0.1%); youth (15-24) unemployment rose +0.5pp to 14.3% and the long-term unemployed share reached 22.5%.
facts.source_title: Statistics Canada — Labour Force Survey, April 2026
connections: Construction employment -16k and information/culture/recreation -25k; health care +18k
Manufacturing employment 244.4k (-2.1% m/m); private-sector job losses ~112,000 YTD 2026

key_developments: Fed held the federal funds target at 3.50%-3.75% on April 29, 2026 (Powell's likely final meeting), in an 8-4 split — the most dissents since October 1992
March U.S. CPI +3.3% YoY; core +2.6%; FOMC statement attributes elevated inflation partly to higher global energy prices
Markets price the 3.50%-3.75% range holding through year-end; Kevin Warsh appointment effective 2026-05-15
global_package.canada_impact: The wide Fed-BoC gap (U.S. 3.50%-3.75% vs Canada 2.25%) supports the USD and caps CAD. Higher U.S. Treasury yields pressure gold and lift GoC yields, contributing to the observed bear-steepening (2Y 3.07%, 10Y 3.70%).

key_developments: Q1 2026 GDP +5.0% YoY, reversing the late-2025 slowdown on strong industrial output and an export surge despite the Iran war
China halting sulfuric-acid exports from May tightens the global copper supply chain
Rebounding Chinese demand a key driver of the copper rally toward record ~US$6.58/lb on May 12
global_package.canada_impact: Resilient Chinese demand supports copper (US$6.32/lb, +36.21% YoY), iron ore and energy export prices, reinforcing strength in 390 Canadian mining projects ($227.11B). Potash and canola channels relevant qualitatively (no timeseries deltas).

key_developments: ECB held its three key rates on April 30, 2026 (deposit 2.00%); upside inflation and downside growth risks described as having intensified
A Bloomberg survey expects two 25bp ECB hikes (June and September) as the Iran war lifts inflation
Energy-driven global inflation regime reinforcing the back-up in global term premia
global_package.canada_impact: Higher European energy-driven inflation and potential ECB tightening support EUR and global yields, reinforcing the Canadian GoC yield back-up and supporting global commodity prices Canada exports.

key_developments: Bank of England held Bank Rate at 3.75% (MPC ending April 29, 2026), an 8-1 vote, a third consecutive no-cut decision
Confirms a synchronized G7 hold/hawkish tilt on energy-led inflation
global_package.canada_impact: The synchronized global hold/hawkish stance on energy-led inflation limits the scope for BoC easing and supports global term-premium repricing reflected in GoC yields.

globalVectors.us: The wide Fed-BoC rate gap (U.S. 3.50%-3.75% vs Canada 2.25%) supports the USD and caps the loonie; higher U.S. Treasury yields lift GoC yields and pressure gold.
globalVectors.china: Q1 2026 China GDP +5.0% and a sulfuric-acid export halt tighten the copper supply chain, supporting Canadian mining export prices (copper +36.21% YoY).
globalVectors.eu: The ECB held the deposit rate at 2.00% with a survey-expected two hikes ahead; energy-driven European inflation supports global commodity prices Canada exports.
